refuter_findings.location: ## Definition, opening setup: spin-structure and gauge-bundle clauses
refuter_findings.evidence: The Definition says “Let P→M be a smooth principal right G-bundle with connection A, let R:G→U(V_R) be a unitary finite-dimensional complex representation, and set E_R=P×_R V_R with its associated Hermitian metric and induced connection.” Its only dependency is def-aqft-thooft-anomaly, which supplies none of these bundle, quotient, Spin-group, or connection definitions. The available mathematical supplier def-associated-bundle-to-a-principal-bundle-and-representation requires a smooth finite-dimensional representation; this Definition neither assumes G is a Lie group nor that R is smooth. Thus the stated induced connection on E_R is not ensured and the setup leaves technical terms undefined.

refuter_findings.location: ## Definition, paragraph immediately after the displayed chiral Dirac map: “Assume the operator is Fredholm.”
refuter_findings.evidence: The Definition says “Assume the operator is Fredholm,” but the item's deps contain only def-aqft-thooft-anomaly. Its proof uses finite-dimensional kernels and cokernels to form the determinant line. The published def-fredholm-operator-cokernel-and-index defines Fredholm for a bounded Banach-space map by closed range and finite-dimensional kernel and cokernel; that definition is absent from this item's dependency closure.

refuter_findings.location: ## Definition, opening paragraph: construction of Q_Y and the boundary reduction
refuter_findings.evidence: The Definition identifies the boundary structure using “the subgroup Spin(d)⊂Spin(d+1) fixing the first frame vector,” but its deps list only def-aqft-global-anomaly-holonomy and def-aqft-thooft-anomaly. Neither defines Spin(n) or the inclusion used to identify the stabilizer. The available def-given-spin-and-spinc-structures-and-associated-spinor-bundles defines Spin(n) via the norm-one even subgroup of the negative-square Clifford algebra and its standard cover, but is not a dependency. The claimed induced boundary Spin(d)-bundle therefore lacks its exact mathematical supplier and subgroup construction.

The Definition allows a “locally compact Hausdorff topological group G” for every 0≤p<d, including non-Abelian G when p>0. But it also requires an effective crossing action with ρ_{gh}=ρ_g∘ρ_h. For standard positive-form symmetries, defects can be deformed past one another, so their crossing actions commute; effectivity then forces gh=hg. Gaiotto, Kapustin, Seiberg, and Willett, Generalized Global Symmetries, §1 PDF p. 3 and §3 PDF p. 11 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1412.5148), state that the group must be Abelian for positive form degree and give the exchange argument. The separate noncommuting-flux discussion in Appendix F does not distinguish or justify a different structure in this Definition.

The item defines the class using “the quotient taken using exactly the model’s admissible four-dimensional background counterterms and total-derivative boundary convention,” but does not define that counterterm set or its mathematical type. The dependency def-qftx-local-brst-cohomology defines H^{g,p}(s|d_H) with denominator {sm+d_Hn: m∈A^{g−1,p}, n∈A^{g,p−1}}. The item substitutes an unspecified model-dependent collection without defining a subspace or equivalence relation compatible with s and d_H, so the claimed quotient and zero-class criterion are not well-defined.

reader_findings.location: ## Definition, opening setup: the spin-structure and gauge-bundle clauses, including the sentence beginning “Let P→M be a smooth principal right G-bundle” and the construction E_R=P×_R V_R.
reader_findings.evidence: The Definition uses Spin(d), a smooth principal right G-bundle with connection, a unitary representation, and an associated complex bundle with induced metric and connection without giving their exact mathematical definitions or citing them as dependencies. reader_findings.location: ## Definition, opening paragraph: the construction of Q_Y using Spin(d+1) and the reduction to the subgroup Spin(d) fixing the first frame vector.
reader_findings.evidence: The Definition names Spin(d+1), Spin(d), their covering maps, and the subgroup inclusion that produces the boundary spin structure, but gives no construction of these groups or the inclusion and has no exact mathematical spin-group dependency. reader_findings.location: ## Definition, group declaration: “A group-like p-form global symmetry … consists of a locally compact Hausdorff topological group G” for all 0≤p<d.
reader_findings.evidence: The definition allows non-Abelian G for p>0. Gaiotto, Kapustin, Seiberg, and Willett, Generalized Global Symmetries, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1412.5148, §1, PDF p. 3, state that the symmetry group must be Abelian for positive form degree. reader_findings.location: ## Definition, local anomaly class paragraph: “with the quotient taken using exactly the model’s admissible four-dimensional background counterterms and total-derivative boundary convention.”
reader_findings.evidence: The item does not define the mathematical type or set of admissible counterterms, nor specify an equivalence relation or subspace compatible with s and d_H. An arbitrary model-specific collection is not automatically the denominator of a relative cohomology group. Define the admissible counterterm space and boundary equivalence, or state the precise quotient construction. The assigned consumer uses this supplier only for the infinitesimal/global scope distinction, not for a vanishing-class inference.
